title: Latency-calibrated embed prober + soft-alias swap for staged model activation
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Background:
Redwood has several embedding onboarding playbooks but we lack a lightweight, automated probe that measures both semantic quality impact on reranking and latency/cost tradeoffs before directing production traffic. Teams frequently run shadow evals and manual analysis; this ticket creates a deterministic embedders + reranker prober (L0 verification) and a soft alias swap mechanism that allows time-boxed, incremental tenant activation with per-tenant traffic budgets and automatic rollback on SLI regressions.

Goals:
- Provide an automated probe that runs candidate embedding models through the reranking endpoint to produce paired quality and latency signals across representative tenant workloads.
- Introduce a soft-alias mechanism (alias names like model:v2-beta) that can receive controlled live traffic percentages per tenant and gracefully fade back to previous model on failure.
- Enforce cost-aware admission: if a new model increases median token-cost or p95 latency beyond configured thresholds, traffic shifts should be throttled or rejected.

Scope (in-scope):
- Implement a probe runner that replays a small set of real tenant queries (anonymized, sampled) to compute: cosine similarity drift, recall@k on reranker test sets, rerank MRR delta, p50/p95 generation latency including embedding compute and reranker scoring, and estimated token-cost delta.
- Build a soft-alias routing layer in the embed gateway that supports per-tenant traffic budgets (0-100%), time-boxed activations, and automatic fallback triggers.
- Hook probe output into rollout decision engine to gate progressive traffic increases (e.g., 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%).
- Add dashboards and SLO alerts: semantic drift > X, MRR drop > Y, p95 latency delta > Z.

Out of scope (for this ticket):
- Large-scale catalog reversion tooling or tenant billing adjustments.
- New model quantization or kernel-level optimizations.

Design notes:
- Probe runner: lightweight container that pulls a curated set of tenant queries from snapshot storage, calls embeddings candidate model and current live model, and posts paired vectors to reranker sandbox to compute downstream metrics. Runs as a scheduled job and on-demand via Console.
- Metrics: cosine_delta_distribution (per-tenant), rerank_mrr_delta, request_latency_embedding(p50/p95), request_latency_reranker(p50/p95), estimated_token_cost_delta. All metrics emitted with tags: model_candidate, model_live, tenant_id_cohort, probe_run_id.
- Soft-alias: a name-level indirection in the embed gateway (model alias metadata) that maps alias -> model-version and routing weight per tenant. We will add a timebox field and auto-fallback rules. Alias changes are stored in the control plane and audited.
- Rollout policy: 1% for 2 hours, then 5% for 6 hours, 20% for 24 hours, then 100% if no rollforward triggers. Rollback triggers: rerank_mrr_delta < -0.02 for any major tenant cohort OR p95 latency delta > +200ms OR estimated_token_cost_delta > +15%.

Telemetry & observability:
- New Console dashboard: "Embed Prober Runs" (trend of cosine_delta, MRR, latencies), "Alias Rollouts" (per-tenant progress bars), and a per-model health page that surfaces probe run history.
- Alerts: severity=page if MRR drop threshold exceeded for >=10 minutes for >5% of active traffic; otherwise Ops-notification channel.

Acceptance criteria:
- Probe runner exists and can be scheduled from Console or triggered via a new internal API endpoint.
- Probe run computes and emits the metrics listed, and they appear in the metrics pipeline within 5 minutes of run completion.
- Soft-alias routing supports per-tenant weight configuration and timebox window; a test alias can be activated for a selected tenant cohort and observe actual traffic split.
- Rollout engine correctly applies the staged percentages and enforces rollback triggers automatically within the configured timebox.
- Documentation: runbook for activating an alias, rollback steps, and a how-to for evaluating probe results included in the ticket.

Manual smoke tests:
- Run probe on a synthetic tenant set; verify cosine deltas and rerank MRR are computed and visible in dashboard.
- Create an alias that sends 10% of tenant "beta-cohort" traffic to candidate model; observe token-cost and latency metrics.
- Force a regression in the reranker sandbox and validate that the rollout engine reverts traffic to the live model.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Prober accidentally leaks PII. Mitigation: only run against anonymized, sampled queries stored in snapshot bucket; require security signoff before enabling live tenant sampling.
- Risk: Misconfigured alias could route too much traffic. Mitigation: default to safe limits (max 1% by UI), require 2-approver flow for >20% activations.

Next steps:
- Spike: 2-day spike to implement a minimal probe that runs local reranker scoring and emits metrics (assigned to Marco).
- Implementation plan: gateway change (alias routing), probe runner, rollout engine hooks, dashboards, runbook.
acceptance_criteria: Probe runner can be scheduled and invoked; emits cosine_delta_distribution, rerank_mrr_delta, embedding_latency_p50_p95, reranker_latency_p50_p95, estimated_token_cost_delta
Metrics are ingested and visible in Console within 5 minutes of run completion
Control plane supports alias -> model-version mapping with per-tenant weight and timebox fields
Rollout engine enforces staged percentages and automatically rolls back on configured triggers
Documentation: runbook + how-to for Console users included in ticket
